{{one source |date=May 2024}}
In algebra, an '''integrable module''' (or '''integrable representation''') of a [[Kac–Moody algebra]] <math>\mathfrak g</math> (a certain [[infinite-dimensional Lie algebra]]) is a [[representation of a Lie algebra|representation]] of <math>\mathfrak g</math> such that (1) it is a sum of weight spaces and (2) the Chevalley generators <math>e_i, f_i</math> of <math>\mathfrak g</math> are [[locally nilpotent endomorphism|locally nilpotent]].<ref>{{harvnb|Kac|1990|loc=§ 3.6.}}</ref> For example, the [[adjoint representation of a Lie algebra|adjoint representation]] of a Kac–Moody algebra is [[integrable]].<ref>{{harvnb|Kac|1990|loc=Lemma 3.5.}}</ref>
